sections.description: SEO score reads what Rank Math reads; liquid theme switch.
sections.changelog:
v1.4.0-dev.179 — Dev

  • MV's SEO score reads the post's ACF text fields as Rank Math's own editor does, so the two agree.
  • Content Studio's light/dark switch is liquid: the knob stretches like a drop, and the new theme pours across the studio from the switch.

v1.4.0-dev.178 — Dev

  • Content Studio's View, Light / Dark, Preview and Focus buttons are icon-only, each named in a tooltip and for screen readers, with a visible keyboard focus.
  • Relationship field entries show their names again.

v1.4.0-dev.177 — Dev

  • Saving a Bricks theme style from MV no longer moves its body and heading typography into link typography.
  • Changing a theme style's conditions takes it off (or puts it on) the builder canvas at once; download size errors name the limit.

v1.4.0-dev.176 — Dev

  • Mimam's Bar's field clears cleanly after applying a command, without the old command drawn over it.
  • Content Studio user fields show the person's name, and their picker lists people instead of posts.

v1.4.0-dev.175 — Dev

  • Code Studio "Site only" CSS no longer loads inside the builder, and Code Studio CSS now loads after Bricks' own styles, so a page override of an MV variable works on the site.
  • Code Studio shows each item's own text after switching items; picking Mimam's Bar from MV's shortcut list opens it; a Media Studio sub-collection keeps its parent.

v1.4.0-dev.174 — Dev

  • Headings pasted with a text direction no longer make the block editor say "Block contains unexpected or invalid content"; posts already affected are repaired on their next Content Studio save.
  • WhatsApp link previews get a share image under 300 KB: the largest copy of the same picture, instead of the full-size file.

v1.4.0-dev.173 — Dev

  • A colour family brought in from Advanced Themer now follows its base: change primary in MV or in Bricks and its shades, tints and transparencies go with it.
  • Saving in MV's Bricks Settings on Bricks' own settings page updates that page's form straight away, so Bricks' Save no longer puts the old values back.

v1.4.0-dev.172 — Dev

  • A variable changed in Bricks' own panel now flows back into MV, and an old copy in an open builder no longer undoes an MV change.
  • When both changed before catching up, the newer change wins and MV's Variables panel tells you.

v1.4.0-dev.171 — Dev

  • Content Studio can edit a post's Rank Math schema as a form, without ever changing its shape.

v1.4.0-dev.170 — Dev

  • Saving in MV's Bricks Settings applies the change in the open builder and canvas straight away, with no reload.

v1.4.0-dev.169 — Dev

  • A variable you save stays saved, even if the Variables list was still loading on a slow connection.

v1.4.0-dev.168 — Dev

  • Switching Mimam's Var off while a workspace page is open in Bricks now really stops the builder saving to the live site.

v1.4.0-dev.167 — Dev

  • Content Studio's import field list shows only the chosen post type's fields, in headed groups.
  • Searchable dropdowns keep their search box pinned while the list scrolls.

v1.4.0-dev.166 — Dev

  • Publishing a workspace in Bricks' file CSS mode no longer leaves the builder you are still in without styles.
  • A publish that worked says so, instead of asking you to settle something.

v1.4.0-dev.165 — Dev

  • Deleting your last global class inside a workspace now sticks, even on a site that never had any.
  • Content Studio's import sample names the post type it is for, so the importer picks it up.

v1.4.0-dev.164 — Dev

  • Media Studio refuses, up front and in plain words, a link that redirects into a private or internal address.

v1.4.0-dev.163 — Dev

  • A workspace page opened in Bricks shows the workspace's variables, classes and palette, not the live site's.
  • The line under Publish says what the check found — pages and global settings — instead of "nothing has changed".

v1.4.0-dev.162 — Dev

  • The import file picks its own post type — from a post_type column, from which type's fields its columns are, or from its name.
  • Columns that are fields of that type are mapped to them, instead of left on Ignore.

v1.4.0-dev.161 — Dev

  • Inside a workspace, MV now refuses to change its own variables instead of letting the change reach your live site, and tells you why and what to do instead. Bricks' own Variables panel works inside a workspace and is held privately.
  • Outside a workspace, MV's Variables panel saves exactly as before.

v1.4.0-dev.160 — Dev

  • Opening a workspace page in Bricks now puts you inside that workspace, and opening an ordinary page takes you back out. Until now nothing ever did, so changes to shared things — variables, classes, theme styles — went straight to the live site.
  • Not yet held: a variable changed through MV's own Variables panel still reaches the live site. That is the next build.

v1.4.0-dev.159 — Dev

  • A heading that was pasted in as styled text with no heading around it is put back inside its heading on save, so the editor stops refusing it. The pasted styling is kept.

v1.4.0-dev.158 — Dev

  • A column mapped to a custom field that will not be created now says "Saved, but no field made" instead of offering nothing. The value is written either way; the setting only controls whether a real field is made for it.
  • Pressing that warning turns the setting on, and the field-type dropdown appears on the same row.

v1.4.0-dev.157 — Dev

  • A colour saved on a variable now shows on the canvas straight away. The value was always saved; the canvas was not being told, so it kept the old colour until a reload.
  • The function that tells it had been written twice, and the shorter copy was silently winning. Nothing in the panel may be declared twice now.

v1.4.0-dev.156 — Dev

  • The custom fields you already have are offered when mapping an import column. They were being fetched from the server and then dropped before anything could show them, so only "New custom field" appeared.
  • The same fault was emptying the kind-of-field picker, so that works again too. An image or file field is offered as a media destination, so a URL lands as an attachment rather than as text.

v1.4.0-dev.155 — Dev

  • A heading block that had a picture wrapped in with it is split apart on save, so the editor stops refusing it. The picture keeps its place.
  • A heading block that only ever held a heading is passed through untouched, down to its blank lines.

v1.4.0-dev.154 — Dev

  • The Workspaces panel scrolls to its end. Its rows were being squashed to fit and hiding the rest, so nothing ever overflowed and there was never anything to scroll - Discard was drawn below the bottom of its own row.
  • Collapsed rows were being trimmed too, which was cutting the workspace names.

v1.4.0-dev.153 — Dev

  • A heading block the editor refused is repaired on save. WordPress assumes a heading is level 2 unless told otherwise, so a stored H1 with no level recorded is a block it cannot rebuild - which is what "Block contains unexpected or invalid content" was.
  • One save on an affected post clears it. A heading whose recorded level disagrees with its tag is corrected too; an ordinary H2 is left alone.

v1.4.0-dev.152 — Dev

  • The Workspaces panel now ends on the screen. Its foot used to hang 68 pixels below the bottom edge of the window, so the last rows could not be reached however far you scrolled.
  • Every floating panel is now as tall as the room below where it starts, so dragging one down makes it shorter instead of pushing its foot off the screen.

v1.4.0-dev.151 — Dev

  • An image keeps the size it was saved at. The attachment id is recovered from the picture's own address when the block has none, and written back, so resaving keeps it.
  • The route from a resized copy back to its upload was measured on a running WordPress: a big upload is filed under -scaled while its copies are not, so the dimensions come off and -scaled goes on.
  • Nothing is guessed - a picture from another site, a deleted file, or a block that already carries an id are all left alone.

v1.4.0-dev.150 — Dev

  • The editor can open a post on the site. A View button beside Preview and Focus, opening it in a new tab. A post that is not published says so rather than promising a page visitors can see, and one that has never been saved offers nothing, because it has no address yet.

v1.4.0-dev.149 — Dev

  • After a publish, the count beside the list and the list itself are read together and read from the site. The counts were awaited and the list was not, so the screen could draw the new number next to the old rows — and both went through the store, which a reload after a write has nothing to gain from.

v1.4.0-dev.148 — Dev

  • The Workspaces Publish strip was drawing a warning where it meant a state. The sentence beside it borrowed the amber callout, and the word Publish was given as much of the row as the sentence, so it wrapped three times into what was left. It is now a heading and its button — the same shape as “In this workspace / Add a page” above it — with where the workspace stands on its own line beneath.
  • Two notices slice 12 added had the same fault and move with it: they were drawing a card inside a card.

v1.4.0-dev.147 — Dev

  • The editor no longer says “Saved” over unsaved changes. The badge had five states and four words: unsaved fell through to Saved. The pill turned amber and said Saved while it did it.
  • And the button says what pressing it would do. It was labelled from the status chosen in the rail rather than the one the site has, so picking Published relabelled it to Update over a post that was still a draft. Between the two, an editor could show a published post that had never been sent anywhere.
  • This is C175. Reproduced against a real WordPress with a real database: MV’s publish route is correct and always was — a draft becomes published and the list says so. What was wrong was everything the screen said about it.

v1.4.0-dev.146 — Dev

  • The Workspaces panel scrolls. Its body was a flex child with none of the three things one needs to become scrollable, so instead of scrolling it simply grew past the bottom of the panel — measured at 1732px of content in a 752px panel, with the last 980px unreachable. Slice 12 made it taller and tipped it over; the panel could have done this with any workspace open.

v1.4.0-dev.145 — Dev

  • A publish that stops halfway can now be finished or put back. Every previous value used to live in PHP memory until the publish ended, so a timeout, a fatal or a killed process left pages changed on the site with no record of which ones or what they had been. Each one is written to the release before it is touched. MV then reads the live pages themselves, says exactly what is on the site, and offers both answers.
  • And it refuses both if anything has been changed by somebody else since. No buttons at all, the item named, and what to do instead.
  • Uninstall tells three things apart. Deactivating deletes nothing. Uninstalling keeps your data by default, recoverable if you reinstall. Removing everything is opt-in, confirmed, and lists what would go and what it would never touch — your published site, native Bricks state, and recovery points.
  • A removal check, before any of it. Active workspaces, unpublished changes, release records, and the sentence that matters: no workspace will be automatically published or rolled back.
  • Deleting the plugin folder is a supported way to remove MV. No hook of MV’s needs to fire for the site to keep showing its last published state.

v1.4.0-dev.144 — Dev

  • .woff files import. They never had: the font reader opens a WOFF only when it is handed a decompressor, and MV handed it none, so every .woff dropped on that panel came back “Read woff error” — under a box asking for them by name. MV now unpacks the WOFF itself before reading it. Checked against every .woff in the repository: same names, same weights, same glyphs as the compressed original.
  • One file that cannot be read no longer loses the others. Eight files where one was damaged used to become a single sentence about none of them. The ones that read are queued, and the one that did not is named.
  • A file named .woff that is not one is told so — a renamed TTF, or a macOS resource-fork stub.

v1.4.0-dev.143 — Dev

  • A publish that does not publish now says so. WordPress does not report a refused status: it saves what it is willing to save and hands the post back as if nothing happened, so Content Studio said “Content updated” and went green over a post that was still a draft. It now compares what it asked for with what landed, names the reason where WordPress gives one — a date still in the future, an account that cannot publish — and points at the site where it does not.
  • The editor rail’s tabs are icons. Publish, SEO, Fields and Block were four text tabs in a three-column strip, so Block wrapped onto a row that was cut off. Four icons fit across, each keeping its name for the tooltip.
  • The font specimen lines up with the family name. It used to start at the card’s edge, a caret’s width to the left of the name above it.
  • And you can set the specimen. Type in it to change the sentence under every family, and pick which cut each family is shown in. The sentence is remembered. Until now the panel drew whichever variant happened to have a file first, which on a library like yours is a thin italic — so every specimen was leaning.

v1.4.0-dev.142 — Dev

  • The Font Manager opens again. In dev.141 it showed “Loading Bricks fonts…” and never stopped: the library was never asked for, and the spinner had no way down. It is asked for, and the spinner now comes down whatever happens.
  • A library that cannot be read says so, and offers Try again. Rather than showing an empty font list, which would not be true.
  • Adobe fonts stay in the typography dropdown. Bricks builds that list in four groups — Adobe, custom, Google, standard — and dev.141 rebuilt three of them, so importing a font through MV emptied the Adobe group until the page was reloaded. MV now keeps the list it was handed and replaces only the custom part.
  • Telling Bricks about a new font can no longer break the import that added it. If that call fails, the import, merge, rename or delete still finishes.

v1.4.0-dev.141 — Dev

  • Library, Import and the search stay where you can reach them. They were inside the scrolling list, so six families down they were gone.
  • A font family starts closed. Click its name to open it. Eighteen weights of Urbanist were eighteen rows between you and the next family; now every family is one line until you ask for more.
  • Bricks sees an imported font without a refresh. Bricks builds its font list once, when the builder loads, so anything imported afterwards was invisible to it until you reloaded the page. MV hands it the new list — after an import, a merge, a rename, and after removing a variant or trashing a family, so a font you deleted stops being offered too.
  • Import has one way back instead of two. The Back to library button is gone; the Library tab does that, and it is on screen at all times now.

v1.4.0-dev.140 — Dev

  • Font import progress stays visible while you inspect the queue. The whole Font Manager used to scroll, so going up to check an early file also scrolled away the only evidence that a 44-file import was still moving. The queue scrolls on its own now; the count, current filename, progress bar, Clear, and Import actions remain in a separate bottom dock without covering the last row.
  • The changing progress is announced once. The count and filename are a polite status; the visual track stays decorative to assistive technology.

v1.4.0-dev.139 — Dev

  • Choosing eighteen fonts really does import eighteen now. The last build sent the ticked items to the picker, except the ticks are held as ids and the picker wanted files — so it failed quietly and fell back to the one file in the details pane. The fix shipped and changed nothing you could see.
  • Skip it skips. It dropped the file and then resumed the import, and the resumed import was reading the queue from before the drop — so it met the same file again. It is handed the queue your answer made.

v1.4.0-dev.138 — Dev

  • Choosing eighteen fonts now imports eighteen fonts. The picker kept one selection and the button only ever handed it the file in the details pane, so a whole ticked set arrived as one. It says how many it is sending now.
  • The refusal carries its answers. It prints at the foot of the panel and the row it is about can be forty rows up, so Replace it, Skip it and Show the file are on the message itself — and the queue scrolls to the row when it stops.
  • And the row was describing the file wrongly. It read Thin · 100 while the refusal read already has Weight · 250. Google’s static fonts do not weigh in hundreds — Roboto SemiCondensed Thin and Extra Light both arrive at 250, which is why the second was refused as a duplicate of the first. A weight that is not one of the nine is read from the font’s own name, and any weight can now be shown and chosen.

v1.4.0-dev.137 — Dev

  • A refused font now asks you something you can answer. It said “Confirm replacement first” and there was nowhere to confirm it — the flag it wanted has been in the request since the import existed and never had a control. The row it stopped on is marked, and carries Replace it and Skip it. Either one carries straight on with the rest.
  • And that font was not a duplicate. Roboto SemiCondensed ExtraLight Italic was being refused for clashing with Roboto ExtraLight Italic. Bricks files a font by weight and style only, so two widths of one family are the same slot to it. A width is part of the family name now — Roboto SemiCondensed — however the font happens to write it.
  • A row that is about to overwrite something says so before it does.
  • And the Font Manager stays where it is when you open the Media Library. It used to close, so you picked a font and then had to find your way back to see it queued. MV keeps one panel open at a time, and the picker was not naming who to return to.

v1.4.0-dev.136 — Dev

  • Font Manager opens with your fonts in it. It said “Bricks Custom Fonts is unavailable” until you refreshed. The panel was answered by a prefetch that had its own idea of what a font family is — it read a setting nothing has ever written, so the answer was always an empty list, and an empty list with nothing to say about Bricks reads as Bricks being missing.
  • An import says how far it has got. Twelve files go in one at a time, and the panel used to sit on “Importing…” for all of it with no way to tell working from stuck. There is a count, a bar, and the queue empties as each one lands.
  • And if one of them is refused, it says which. What went in stays in, what is left in the queue is exactly what did not, so pressing Import again carries on instead of sending the first ones twice.
  • The same fault, found in one more place. The custom-tag list was prefetched without the tidying the real answer does, so a tag could look one way for a moment and another way after.

v1.4.0-dev.135 — Dev

  • One font family now imports as one font family. Importing Inter produced eight of them — Inter 28pt, Inter 28pt Light, Inter 28pt SemiBold and so on. A static font has to write its weight into its family name for applications that can only hold four styles, and MV was reading that name instead of the one the designer gave it.
  • And the ones already split can be put back together. The library spots families that differ only by a weight word and offers to merge them into the one you kept. The others go to Trash, where Bricks can restore them, and every font file stays in the Media Library.
  • Delete asks where you pressed it. The confirmation was pinned to the top of the list, so pressing the trash on a family halfway down looked like nothing had happened — the question was open, several hundred pixels above you. It is drawn inside the family now. So is the editor.
  • Import can take a font the site already has. Media Library sits beside Choose files, and importing from it links the file you picked rather than uploading a second copy of it.

v1.4.0-dev.134 — Dev

  • Publishing a workspace now actually publishes its globals. Slices 7 to 10 isolated sixteen of them and held every change — and nothing ever put them back. A variable changed in a workspace was kept safely and then kept for ever. Anything that asked you to publish and confirm a variable change had reached the site could not have passed.
  • And the next page load no longer undoes it. Publishing makes the live value equal the workspace’s, which is exactly what MV’s leak detector is built to spot — it would have put the old value back within minutes. The workspace lets go of what it published, so there is nothing left to mistake for a leak.
  • A conflict can be answered. When a global changed in your workspace AND on the site, publishing is now blocked until you choose: keep mine, keep the site’s, or skip it this time. Answering never changes the site by itself.
  • Publish refuses rather than shipping a hole. If a page needs a template or an image that exists nowhere — or a template still in draft — publishing stops and names it, instead of putting a page live that renders nothing.
  • And it publishes in the right order, so a template lands before the page that pulls it in.
  • And you can now answer that conflict where you see it. The publish card shows the globals that will go out by name, the ones you left out, and what the pages need — with Keep mine, Keep the site’s and Skip it on the conflict itself. Answering never changes the site.
  • A workspace where you only changed a variable can be published at all. It used to answer “nothing has changed” and offer to publish 0 pages, because it counted only pages — which is the exact case this build is about.
  • And a publish still either happens or does not. If a page fails its check, the pages AND the global settings go back to what they were, and your workspace is holding its change again — rather than half of it being live.
  • A publish that was refused no longer takes your workspace’s styling with it. Blocking on a conflict used to delete the workspace’s own stylesheets, so the next edit you made was styled by the live site instead of by your workspace.

v1.4.0-dev.133 — Dev

  • Bricks 2.4: a workspace leak, closed. 2.4 gives variables a trash, the way classes have had one. MV’s workspace overlay did not know about it — so trashing a variable inside a workspace wrote it straight to the live site while MV went on saying the workspace was isolated. Nothing errored; it just leaked.
  • Two Bricks settings MV offered no longer exist. 2.4 removed Check for corrupt data and Template thumbnail height outright. MV was still showing both and writing keys nothing reads.
  • MV now warns when it cannot do what it claims. 2.4’s new Abilities API writes global design options straight to the database, so MV’s workspace hold is not in that path at all. It is off by default; with it on, the workspace panel says plainly that design changes made through it reach the live site immediately.
  • And the workspace panel stopped telling you something untrue. It still said global classes, variables and theme styles were not held — that has not been true since dev.126.
  • Checked, not assumed: all 35 Bricks classes, methods and constants MV calls still exist in 2.4; the builder JS API is unchanged; theme style controls are identical; and the CSS-file mechanism slice 10 rests on still works the way it did.

v1.4.0-dev.132 — Dev

  • A column can now be pointed at a custom field you already have. The destination list used to end at one generic Custom field, and that always wrote a meta key named after the column — so on a site whose fields are already built, a column called why_this_matters had no way of reaching a field called role_description. Every field on the site is now in the list, searchable, labelled by name and key.
  • Or given a name you choose. New custom field, name it… opens a box; Enter accepts, Escape closes. The plain option now says which key it would use rather than leaving you to guess.
  • An image or file field is offered as a media destination, so a column of URLs downloads into it instead of writing the URL in as text, which is what those fields cannot read.
  • Two things this found on the way. The kind-of-field picker added last build was rendering outside the mapping row’s grid, in the status column. And the row could promise a key WordPress would not write — it strips characters it cannot use rather than replacing them, so a column headed “Why this matters” becomes whythismatters. The row says so now.
  • Every mapping saved before this still means what it meant.

v1.4.0-dev.131 — Dev

  • Structure now shows only taxonomy definitions Content Studio owns. Plugin/theme taxonomies are hidden from both Structure lists instead of occupying the editor as read-only rows.
  • Content editing keeps its assigned taxonomies. External taxonomy terms remain available where posts and custom content actually use them.

v1.4.0-dev.130 — Dev

  • The four Folders are four different structures. Taxonomies registered by another plugin or the theme now show their assigned content type, real taxonomy key, and ownership instead of repeating one ambiguous label.
  • External taxonomy definitions are read-only here. ACF-owned taxonomies retain edit, duplicate, and delete; Content Studio cannot accidentally offer an ACF save form for a structure owned elsewhere.
  • Structure editors end at their own footer. The normal content records table is unmounted while a post type, taxonomy, options page, field group, category view, or create form is open, so its empty header cannot remain attached below the editor.

v1.4.0-dev.129 — Dev

  • Workspaces slice 10 — workspaces now work with Bricks set to load CSS from files. Slices 7 to 9 refused to run in that mode. A workspace now gets its own copy of the site’s stylesheets, seeded from the live ones when you open it and rebuilt by Bricks’ own generators as you work, so you see your changes and the site keeps its own files untouched.
  • The reason for the old refusal turned out to be wrong. It said Bricks rewrites the shared stylesheets on save; in this version every one of those is triggered by the option write, and MV was already holding that. So the workspace was never leaking into the site’s CSS — it was showing you the site’s styling instead of your own.
  • Publishing rebuilds the real stylesheets once, after the change lands, and takes the workspace’s copies away with it.
  • MV asks in MV’s own voice now. Three places still opened a browser dialog — closing comments everywhere, deleting a capability, naming a new one. One of them was printing a stray \n\n on screen. All three are MV dialogs, and nothing in the panel calls the browser’s any more.
  • Content import: choose the kind of custom field. A column mapped as Custom field had its type guessed from its own values with no way to say otherwise — and a column of 1s and 0s is a true/false or a number, with no way for the file to say which. Pick the kind on the column, or leave it on Detect.
  • And the sample CSV imports as it comes. Its image and audio URLs were placeholders that could never download. They are real files now.

v1.4.0-dev.128 — Dev

  • Workspaces slice 9 — every global the builder saves is now isolated, not just variables. Global classes and their categories, locked and trashed lists, theme styles, components, global elements, the colour palette, style manager, global queries and pseudo classes. Change any of them in a workspace and you see your change; the site does not, until you publish.
  • Emptying your last global class no longer deletes the site’s. Bricks deletes the option rather than saving an empty one, and WordPress offers nothing that can stop a delete — so MV puts it straight back in the same request, and you still see the empty list you asked for.
  • Bricks’ own “somebody else changed these classes” warning now agrees with your workspace instead of firing over your own unsaved work. Its timestamp moves with the classes it belongs to.
  • And your workspace no longer rewrites the site’s CSS files. Holding the option write also stops Bricks regenerating the shared stylesheets — and MV’s own theme-styles screen, which regenerated one directly, now stands down inside a workspace.

v1.4.0-dev.127 — Dev

  • Workspaces slice 8 — if MV stops while a builder tab is open, the leak is found and undone. Opening a workspace now records what the live variables say. If the plugin is switched off (or killed, or its folder deleted) and a stale Bricks tab saves, that value lands on the live site with nothing to hold it. On MV’s next admin request it is detected, the live value is put back, the work stays in the workspace, and you are told what was live and for how long.
  • It never guesses. If the live value is neither the recorded one nor the workspace’s, MV cannot tell a leak from somebody’s legitimate edit — so it changes nothing and raises a conflict instead. A wrong repair would destroy real work, which is worse than the leak.
  • And it can prove MV was away. Every live write MV is running for is recorded as witnessed. So an edit another admin made while MV was up is never undone, even when it happens to match your workspace exactly.
  • The builder stops saving when MV stops answering. While a workspace is open the builder asks MV every few seconds; if MV goes quiet, Save and ⌘S are blocked and the builder says why. Best-effort on purpose — it is why the repair above exists.
  • In file CSS-loading mode none of this runs. Slice 7 already stands its overlay down there, so a workspace never diverges from Live and flagging every ordinary edit as drift would make the feature unusable. Switching to file mode after opening a workspace is safe too — an earlier recording is not acted on afterwards.
  • The workspace base is never quietly moved. Drift is reported once, not on every page load, and noticing a change never becomes accepting it.

v1.4.0-dev.126 — Dev

  • Workspaces slice 7 — Bricks variables are isolated inside a workspace. Change a variable while you are working in a workspace and you see your change; a visitor, and anyone not in that workspace, sees the live value. The change is kept in the workspace and reaches the site only when you publish.
  • Nothing is written to the site while you work. The live option row is not touched and neither is the object cache — proved against WordPress’s own option API rather than assumed, because a write during a workspace session is the one path that could put a draft value in front of a visitor.
  • It fails towards Live, always. Before WordPress knows who is asking, in file CSS-loading mode, on a workspace that has been published or discarded, or when the workspace has not touched variables at all — every one of those serves the live value.
  • What this does not claim: isolation lasts while MV runs. Switch the plugin off and every request sees the live option again. A workspace page is a private draft and stays hidden without MV; a variable is not.

v1.4.0-dev.125 — Dev

  • The import can create the fields it needs. Turn on Create missing fields and any column mapped as a custom field gets a real field definition — in ACF or JetEngine, in a new group MV makes or one you already have. Off by default.
  • The type is read from the column, never from its name. Image URLs make an Image, a PDF or an MP3 a File, other links a URL, addresses an Email, yes/no a True / False, dates a Date Picker, numbers a Number, a short repeating set a Select with those choices, long text a Textarea. One row that disagrees drops the column to a type that can hold both — a type that is right for most rows is wrong for the column.
  • And the things it refuses to guess. A column of 1s and 0s stays a Number, because nothing in it says it is a flag and a checkbox would destroy the difference between 0 and empty. A column that already has a field is left exactly as it is.

v1.4.0-dev.124 — Dev
